name: The American Historical Review
description: Articles for the American Historical Review: Times New Roman 12, double-spaced, on letter paper with one-inch margins; no headings, only section breaks; all references in footnotes of 10 points, with no bibliography; fully anonymised.

source.name: American Historical Association, AHR article submission page and Style Sheet for Article Authors
source.notes: The submission page was read live and in a snapshot of 2026-07-10, which agree; the style sheet was read in a snapshot of 2026-03-12. The journal uses NO headings or subheadings, only section breaks marked with #: the heading levels here are the general default and should not be used. Not specified, and taken from the general default: alignment, paragraph indent (the source says only that there is no space between paragraphs), the block-quotation threshold and form, the position of page numbers (pages must be numbered), line numbers. The title page is uploaded as a file of its own, before the main document; the abstract and keywords are entered in the submission form and not in the manuscript, so no abstract is shown. No bibliography or list of works cited is wanted: the bibliography values are the general default. One note per sentence, at its end; notes are not for building on the argument. Reference style: a house style that 'generally follows' the Chicago Manual, 17th ed., notes form, which is given here; the house style adds 'here' before the page cited within a range, and says that the publisher is omitted from book citations, though three of its four examples of books include one. Figures and tables go in separate files; at most 8 figures.

limits.note: At most 8,000 words, not counting notes, tables and charts; footnotes should be between 4,000 and 5,000 words. Abstract of 150-200 words and four or five keywords, entered in the submission form.
